title: McMinnville Trent photos

tellings.quote: but there's no way to ultimately debunk it. It's unfalsifiable in either direction. And Paul and Evelyn Trent were these hapless farmers.
In the case of McMinnville and Lake Coat, we have video.
tellings.difference: Does not name the Trents, and groups the case with Lake Cote as cases with video.
tellings.link_reason: Same 1950 McMinnville, Oregon UFO photographs, told by the same host.

related.note: Both are about the 1950 McMinnville Trent photos. This telling says a string was revealed at a French conference, which makes them a hoax, while the story calls them unfalsifiable.

plain: A podcast host, Jesse Michels, talks about photos that a farming couple, Paul and Evelyn Trent, are said to have taken of something in the sky near their home in McMinnville, Oregon, around 1950. Michels calls the Trents "hapless farmers" and says the case can't be finally proved or disproved either way, and on another show he groups it with a case at Lake Cote as one where there is a visual record. Supporters bring it up because, if the pictures show what they seem to, they would be early photographic evidence of an unknown craft.
